questions.question: Before driving, how do you make sure air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for air escaping.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Let air pressure build up, then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching the whole vehicle.

questions.question: What should a driver do to prevent a rollover?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly. To prevent rollovers, keep the vehicle's center of gravity low. Load cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
A valve that shows the fuel level
A valve that measures air brake system liquid
A valve that releases extra pressure from the braking system

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve, also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar, controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: When driving a trailer with ABS, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brakes less than you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake less often than you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a tractor-trailer with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When do large combination vehicles take the longest to stop?
questions.explanation: Large combination vehicles take longer to stop when empty than when loaded. Lower weight means less traction between the wheels and the road.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: Regularly to activate the trailer brakes in all driving conditions.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid.
Only when the trailer is carrying a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the trailer brakes. Do not use it while driving because it may cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before your trip. First make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then test the emergency brakes by pulling out the trailer air supply control or setting it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes so the wheels can regain traction with the road. Once the wheels grip the road again, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what is especially important?

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, make sure there is a large enough gap for you to safely do so.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?

options.text: It will not make a difference when coupling.

questions.explanation: Check that the trailer is at the right height before coupling it to the tractor. If the trailer is too low, the trailer nose may get damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents.
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your truck. Turn corners slowly.

questions.question: When air lines use color coding, which color marks service lines?
questions.explanation: Service lines are blue. Emergency lines are red. These colors help you connect the right lines.

questions.question: When connecting air lines, match the colors. Service lines are often:
questions.explanation: Match colors when connecting air lines. Service lines are blue. Emergency lines are red. Color coding helps prevent mistakes.

questions.question: When a truck with a trailer turns a corner:

options.text: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should go over the curb.
It is okay to knock over street signs if they are too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning. This is called off-tracking. Trailers show this effect more than other vehicles.

questions.question: Trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: Trailers made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: In a truck with an automatic tractor protection valve, when does the valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, it closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: Good coupling technique:

options.text: Is the same for all vehicles.
Means the fifth wheel should not be greased.
Can be learned slowly over time.

questions.explanation: Proper coupling and uncoupling is essential to safe driving of trucks with trailers. Wrong coupling is very dangerous.

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer is skidding is to:

options.text: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left the lane.
Release the brake and then press it again.
Watch for a jackknife warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left the lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer stays in its lane.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check the trailer and tractor connection.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called a trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: Having ABS on just one axle:

options.text: Gives you better control when braking.
Puts extra stress on other axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Having ABS on just the trailer or one axle still helps you control the vehicle better when braking.
